entries.name: Autonomous Circuit
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Describe a board; get a fab-ready PCB with a live board view, ordered from JLCPCB in a click.

entries.name: Autonomous Workshop
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: Describe a part; get a validated, printable STEP with a live 3D view.

entries.name: Blender
entries.author: Blender Foundation
entries.description: Describe an object, a scene, a shot — and watch it take shape: modelled in Blender's Python, rendered headless, exported as glTF you can orbit and zoom in the pane.

examples.prompt: Make a cozy isometric reading nook: a cut-away corner of a room with an armchair, a floor lamp glowing warm, a bookshelf full of colourful books, a round rug and a monstera, with evening sun through the window and a cat asleep on the rug.
examples.caption: Isometric reading nook · 122 named objects, 35 materials · glTF + Cycles render

examples.prompt: Model a small desk robot toy: a rounded body, a head with two round eyes, two arms that rotate at the shoulders, an antenna, and a round base. Separate named objects in collections, real sizes in millimetres, and nice materials.
examples.caption: Desk robot toy · 29 named parts, 10 materials · glTF + Cycles render

entries.name: CAD Viewer
entries.author: Jake Fitzgerald
entries.description: Jake Fitzgerald's CAD Viewer (earthtojake/text-to-cad) as a Harness pane: STEP, GLB, STL, 3MF, DXF, URDF, SRDF and SDF, with MoveIt2 inverse kinematics.

entries.name: CircuitJS
entries.author: Paul Falstad
entries.description: Describe a circuit — an RC filter, a 555 flasher, an amplifier — and watch it run in the pane: charge animating along the wires, scope traces drawing, every value still yours to poke at.

examples.prompt: Build a two-transistor flasher that alternates three red and three blue LEDs like a police light, about twice a second, with a scope on each side and a knob for each side's on-time.
examples.caption: Police-light flasher · two-transistor astable, ~2.2 Hz · 2 scopes + 2 timing knobs

examples.prompt: Build a 555 astable LED flasher with a potentiometer that sets the rate, and scopes on the capacitor and the output.
examples.caption: 555 LED flasher · running live, ~1.1 Hz · rate knob + 2 scopes

entries.name: Doc Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A reader for the PDF a harness is writing: thumbnails, the outline, find, zoom and two-page spreads on pdf.js — redrawn in place on every compile, changed pages marked, compile errors shown over the last good pages.

entries.name: Excalidraw
entries.author: Excalidraw
entries.description: Describe a diagram — an architecture, a flow, a whiteboard sketch — and watch it appear hand-drawn in the pane, as an .excalidraw file you can open anywhere.

examples.prompt: Map an online store's checkout as a flowchart: cart, sign-in or guest checkout, shipping, payment with a declined-card retry loop, a fraud check that can send orders to manual review, then order confirmed and the email receipt. Diamonds for decisions, one frame per stage.
examples.caption: Checkout flowchart · 3 decisions, retry loop, 3 frames · .excalidraw

examples.prompt: Draw the architecture of a URL shortener: browser, CDN, API service, Postgres, Redis cache, a click-tracking worker on a queue, and an analytics dashboard. Frame the backend and label the arrows.
examples.caption: URL shortener architecture · 10 shapes, 8 labeled arrows · .excalidraw

entries.name: Film Viewer
entries.author: OpenHarness contributors
entries.description: A screening room for OpenMontage productions: live storyboards, a film player, render versions, and notes tied to a moment in the cut.

entries.name: Game Viewer
entries.author: OpenHarness contributors
entries.description: A live game studio: playable previews, real build progress, versions, and an uninterrupted last working game while the next one takes shape.

entries.name: Godogen
entries.author: Alex Ermolov
entries.description: Build a world you can play. Watch your game take shape in a live studio, explore each version, and play while the agent keeps creating.

entries.name: Manim
entries.author: Manim Community
entries.description: Describe an explanation — a proof, a transform, an algorithm, a graph — and watch it animate: scenes in Python, rendered by Manim, playing in the pane.

examples.prompt: Draw a chess knight using nothing but spinning circles: a Fourier series of 120 epicycles, tip to tail, tracing its silhouette in gold.
examples.caption: Fourier knight · 120 epicycles · 17 s 1080p60 MP4, 4 chapters

examples.prompt: Animate the Pythagorean theorem in about 20 seconds: draw a 3-4-5 right triangle, grow squares on its three sides with their areas labelled, then show 9 + 16 = 25.
examples.caption: Pythagorean theorem · 20 s animation · 1080p MP4

entries.name: marimo
entries.author: marimo
entries.description: Describe an analysis, a model, a dashboard — and watch the reactive notebook come alive in the pane: marimo's own editor on the notebook the agent writes, cells re-running as it types.

entries.name: Marp
entries.author: Yuki Hattori
entries.description: Describe a talk; get a keynote — huge type, generated art, speaker notes — live in the pane, exported to PDF, PPTX or HTML.

entries.name: 3D Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: A Blender-style viewport for the glTF a harness exports — outliner, properties in mm, shading modes, measure, section, explode, scene camera, timeline — live on every export.

entries.name: MuJoCo
entries.author: Google DeepMind
entries.description: Describe a robot, a scene, a controller — a Unitree quadruped standing, a humanoid learning to walk — and watch the rollout play: MuJoCo physics, Menagerie robots, MJX for training.

examples.prompt: Make the Unitree G1 humanoid say hello: stand, raise its right hand and wave three times, then lower it and take a small bow. Record it.
examples.caption: Unitree G1 humanoid · wave hello + bow · 29 servos, 11 s rollout, live in the MuJoCo Viewer

examples.prompt: Load the Unitree Go2, make it stand, then do three slow squats and wave the front left leg. Record it.
examples.caption: Unitree Go2 · 3 squats + a wave · 21 s rollout, live in the MuJoCo Viewer

entries.name: MuJoCo Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: MuJoCo's own simulate, in the pane: live physics you can push, pull and pause, every actuator on a slider, contacts and forces drawn, sensors plotted, and the agent's recording replayed frame by frame — on MuJoCo's WebAssembly build.

entries.name: OpenMontage
entries.author: calesthio
entries.description: Direct a film from the first idea to the final cut. Watch the script, shots, and edits arrive in a live studio; play each version and leave notes right on the film.

entries.name: Phaser
entries.author: Phaser Studio
entries.description: Describe a game — a breakout, a platformer, a shooter, a puzzle — and play it in the pane as the agent writes it in Phaser 4, reloading on every save.

examples.prompt: Make a side-scrolling platformer at sunset: a little fox runs and double-jumps across floating islands, collects glowing berries, stomps hedgehogs and races to a lantern at the end. Parallax mountains, procedural art only.
examples.caption: Sunset Fox · parallax platformer, 48 berries, double jump · playable in the pane

examples.prompt: Make a small brick breaker game with a title screen, three levels, power-ups that widen the paddle, and a score.
examples.caption: Brick by Brick · 3 levels, wide-paddle power-ups · playable in the pane

entries.name: RDKit
entries.author: RDKit
entries.description: Describe a molecule — a drug, an analogue, a scaffold — and get it designed, its properties computed and a 3D conformer you can rotate in the pane.

entries.name: Remotion
entries.author: Remotion
entries.description: Describe a video — a product launch, an explainer, a data story — and watch it play in Remotion Studio as the agent writes it in React, then render it to MP4.

examples.prompt: Make a 12-second "my year in running" recap video: total kilometres counting up, a glowing route line drawing itself across a city map, and monthly distance bars rising one by one with the best month lit up. Bold type, sunset colours.
examples.caption: Year in running recap · 12 s 1080p MP4 · count-up, route, 12 bars

examples.prompt: Make a 12 second launch video for the Harness Store with three beats: the store opens, a card flips to Get, and a spinning 3D cube lands in a pane. Bold type, smooth motion. Render it to MP4.
examples.caption: Harness Store launch · 12 s 1080p MP4 · 3 beats

entries.name: Strudel
entries.author: Strudel
entries.description: Describe a track — a groove, a bassline, a break — and hear it in the pane. The agent writes one Strudel pattern file; Strudel's own REPL plays it live and hot-swaps on every save.

examples.prompt: Make an 80s synthwave track at 100 bpm: gated drums, a driving octave bassline, a pulsing 16th-note arpeggio, a wide supersaw pad, and a soaring lead that takes over after 8 bars.
examples.caption: Synthwave "Night drive" · 100 bpm, 8 voices, 16 bars · playing live in the pane

examples.prompt: Write a 90 bpm lo-fi house groove: a kick and hats from bar 1, a bassline, warm chords, a hook that enters at bar 9, and a break at bar 17.
examples.caption: Lo-fi house groove · 90 bpm, 9 voices, 32 bars · playing live in the pane

entries.name: text-to-cad
entries.author: Jake Fitzgerald
entries.description: Jake Fitzgerald's text-to-cad skills (earthtojake/text-to-cad), pinned: describe a part, get STEP with mesh exports, drawings, robot files and G-code, live in the CAD Viewer.

entries.name: Typst
entries.author: Typst GmbH
entries.description: Describe a document — a paper, a spec sheet, a report, a letter — and watch the PDF take shape as Typst compiles it on every save.

examples.prompt: Make a two-page orbital mechanics cheat sheet: Kepler's three laws, the vis-viva equation, a labelled diagram of an elliptical orbit, a Hohmann transfer from Earth to Mars worked out step by step, and a table of planet data. Two columns, dense but beautiful.
examples.caption: Orbital mechanics field guide · 2-page PDF, 3 figures, 3 tables

examples.prompt: Write a one-page spec sheet for a 20 mm M3 aluminium hex standoff: a title, a two-sentence description, a table of dimensions (length, across-flats, thread, mass), materials and finish, and a tolerances note. Keep it to one page.
examples.caption: Hex standoff spec sheet · 1-page PDF with drawing and dimension table

entries.name: Video Viewer
entries.author: Autonomous
entries.description: An editor-grade player for what a harness renders: every render listed, chapters on the timeline, frame-accurate scrubbing with a filmstrip, loops and stills — and the render in progress playable as it is made.

entries.name: Web Viewer
entries.author: OpenHarness contributors
entries.description: A live preview for HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a harness workspace. Reloads when files change.

entries.name: Yosys
entries.author: YosysHQ
entries.description: Describe a digital circuit — a counter, a UART, a state machine — and get Verilog, a simulation with waveforms, a synthesized gate-level schematic and an FPGA bitstream for an iCE40 board. Prompt to silicon.

examples.prompt: Build a tiny 8-bit CPU for the iCEBreaker that runs a Fibonacci program from ROM and prints every number over the USB serial port at 115200 baud; the button runs it again. Simulate it, check the serial output in the testbench and build the bitstream.
examples.caption: Tiny 8-bit CPU printing Fibonacci over UART · 8 checks pass · 294 LCs, 26.1 MHz · iCE40 bitstream

examples.prompt: Design a UART transmitter at 115200 baud from the 12 MHz clock that sends the text HELLO followed by newline each time the button is pressed (debounced), plus a breathing PWM on the green LED. Testbench must decode the serial frames and check the bytes. Run the whole flow, keep Fmax above 12 MHz, and report LUTs and Fmax.
examples.caption: HELLO over UART + breathing LED · 25 checks pass · 226 LCs, 51.9 MHz · iCE40 bitstream
